title: Leco language - Wikipedia
text: Leco, also written as Leko, is a language isolate that, though long reported to be extinct, is spoken by 20–40 individuals in areas east of Lake Titicaca, Bolivia. The Leco ethnic population was 13,527 in 2012.

title: Language isolate - Wikipedia
text: A language isolate, sometimes called an isolated language, is a language that has no demonstrable genealogical relationship with any other language. [1][2] That is, an isolate is a language family that only contains one member.

text: Leco Language (Buruwa, Leko) Language: Leco, also known as Buruwa, is a South American language isolate still spoken by only a few older people in western Bolivia.

title: Leco language
text: Leco is an endangered language isolate spoken by approximately 20 to 40 elderly individuals (as of 2001) in the eastern Andean foothills of western Bolivia, primarily in areas east of Lake Titicaca such as the Apolo region and along the Mapiri and Kaka rivers.
